newsitem.title: USA: Marine Drilling day rate up in Q1.
newsitem.headline: Marine Drilling day rate up in Q1.

text.p: Marine Drilling Cos Inc reported record first quarter results saying the day rate for its rigs averaged $32,800 during the quarter, up from $27,500 in the final three months of 1996.

It reported first-quarter net income of $10.2 million, or $0.20 per share, on revenues of $36.8 million. That compares to profits a year earlier of $2.3 million, or $0.05 per share, on revenues of $21.2 million.
"We are very pleased with our first-quarter results," chief executive Jan Rask said.
"During the quarter, our marketed rigs were 100 percent utilized at an average day rate of approximately $32,800 compared with fourth-quarter performance of 100 percent and $27,500, respectively.

Looking forward, we expect continued improvement in operating results during 1997 due to strong drilling market conditions and the expected deployment of the MARINE 15 later this month and the MARINE 305 in the third quarter."

The company also said its most recently acquired rig, the MARINE 500, started operations in Southeast Asia during the first quarter and is contracted through March 1998 at dayrates ranging from $54,000 to $70,000.
